_**Agent (grok-4.7)**_

Lowering the match threshold will not fix picture 1. The matcher is looking at the wrong part of the photo.

Detection assumes the badge fills the viewfinder. It crops that box, stretches it to 200×320, and compares only the bottom 22% with the same strip on each template (Delegate, Official, and the rest). That strip is where the role word sits. A match needs a score of at least 0.52 and a gap of 0.035 over second place.

In picture 2 the card fills the frame, so that bottom strip lands on OFFICIAL and the match succeeds. In picture 1 the card is smaller and there is black screen under it. The bottom 22% is mostly that black area, and DELEGATE has shifted up out of the window. Every template then scores about the same (0.46–0.49). There is no winner to accept. The same thing happens on Take a photo: the whole image is stretched, and the role band is whatever happens to sit at the bottom of the file.

**What to change**

Find the card inside the frame, then run the matcher we already have.

The useful landmark is the dark role bar (DELEGATE, OFFICIAL, and so on). Search the frame for that dark horizontal band under the light card, crop the card from it, and only then take the bottom strip and compare. Picture 1 already shows that bar clearly; it is just higher than the fixed window.

A lighter version of the same idea is to try several vertical positions and scales and keep the alignment with the best score and the best gap. That covers “not zoomed in, still roughly upright and centered,” which is picture 1. It is weaker if the card is tilted or far off to one side.

Leave `0.52` where it is. Dropping it would start accepting background, because those failed frames already sit in a tight cluster with no clear winner.

**What I would not do first**

A general feature matcher or an OCR library is more weight than this needs. The five cards are the same artwork plus one high-contrast word. Locating that bar is enough.

**Suggested order**

1. Locate the dark role bar (or the light card above it) inside the viewfinder crop and inside Take a photo.
2. Classify only that crop with the current comparison.
3. If angled shots still fail after that, add a simple four-corner straighten. Skip that until we see it fail.

I can implement step 1 and 2 next if that matches what you want on the floor.

Yes. Run them as one pipeline on each capture. The scale search from earlier drops out, because locating the card replaces it.

The app is only React today, so this stays inside the capture button. Nothing runs on the live camera.

**Pipeline**

1. **Find the dark role bar** inside the viewfinder, and inside a Take a photo image. That bar is the stable landmark. The five cards share the same artwork and differ only in that word.
2. **Build the four corners from that bar.** The bar is the bottom edge. The card’s aspect ratio is already known from the template images, so the other three corners are projected from the bar’s angle and width. That straightens a mild tilt without a document-scanner library.
3. **Warp** that quad to the same 200×320 canvas the templates use.
4. **Score it twice.** The existing image comparison runs on the role strip. An OCR pass reads that same strip, restricted to `GUEST`, `DELEGATE`, `SPEAKER`, `CREW`, and `OFFICIAL`.

**When they disagree**

| OCR | Image match | Result |
|---|---|---|
| One of the five words | Anything, including a weak score | Accept the OCR word |
| Nothing usable | Clears 0.52 and leads by 0.035 | Accept the image match |
| One word | A different word | Reject |
| Nothing usable | Below the bar, or a tie | Reject |

OCR is allowed to win on a weak image score because picture 1 fails from framing, not from an unreadable word. A disagreement is treated as a miss so a bad read cannot override a clear image match.

**Library**

`tesseract.js` is the practical choice. It runs on both iPhone Safari and Android Chrome. The on-device text detector in Chrome does not exist on iOS, and this scan page has to work on both.

Start the OCR worker when the Scan screen opens, so the first Capture is not waiting on the download. The comparison still works if that download has not finished. OCR joins in once the worker is ready.

Expect a few megabytes of WASM and English trained data, and a few hundred milliseconds per capture on a small crop. That is acceptable on a button press. OpenCV is not worth adding beside it. Corner finding stays a short pass over the role bar.

        sum_b += i*hist[i]
        m_b = sum_b / w_b

    seen = bytearray(w*h)
    best = []

        if not m or seen[i]: continue
        stack = [i]
        seen[i] = 1
        comp = []
        while stack:
            p = stack.pop()
            comp.append(p)
            x = p % w
            y = p // w
            for nx, ny in ((x-1,y),(x+1,y),(x,y-1),(x,y+1)):
                if nx&lt;0 or ny&lt;0 or nx&gt;=w or ny&gt;=h: continue
                j = ny*w+nx
                if mask[j] and not seen[j]:
                    seen[j] = 1
                    stack.append(j)

    return best

    pts = sorted(set(points))
    if len(pts) &lt;= 2: return pts
    def cross(o,a,b):
        return (a[0]-o[0])*(b[1]-o[1]) - (a[1]-o[1])*(b[0]-o[0])
    lower = []
    for p in pts:
        while len(lower) &gt;= 2 and cross(lower[-2], lower[-1], p) &lt;= 0:

        lower.append(p)

    tr = max(points, key=lambda p: p[0]-p[1])

    bl = min(points, key=lambda p: p[0]-p[1])

    tl, tr, br, bl = quad
    # extend side edges beyond bottom by EXTEND * side length
    def push(top, bot):
        dx, dy = bot[0]-top[0], bot[1]-top[1]
        return (bot[0]+dx*EXTEND, bot[1]+dy*EXTEND)
    return tl, tr, push(tr, br), push(tl, bl)

def locate(im, analysis=180):
    im = im.convert(&#39;RGB&#39;)
    scale = analysis / im.width
    small = im.resize((analysis, max(1,int(im.height*scale))), Image.BILINEAR)
    data, w, h = luma_img(small)
    th = otsu(data)
    # light is the bright class; if otsu splits poorly, bias toward paper
    mask = [1 if v &gt; th else 0 for v in data]
    light_frac = sum(mask)/len(mask)
    comp = largest_cc(mask, w, h)
    if len(comp) &lt; 0.05*w*h:
        return None, th, light_frac, 0
    # subsample boundary-ish points: use all pixels if small, else every pixel of component is ok at 180px
    pts = [(i%w, i//w) for i in comp]
    # convex hull of component — use a stride if huge
    step = max(1, len(pts)//4000)
    hpts = hull(pts[::step])
    c = corners(hpts)
    quad = extend(c)
    # scale back
    inv = 1/scale
    quad = tuple((x*inv, y*inv) for x,y in quad)
    return quad, th, light_frac, len(comp)/(w*h)

def quad_area(q):
    area = 0
    for i in range(4):
        x1,y1 = q[i]
        x2,y2 = q[(i+1)%4]
        area += x1*y2 - x2*y1
    return abs(area)/2

_**Agent (grok-4.7)**_

A badge no longer has to fill the frame. Capture and Take a photo both find the card, straighten it, then read the role two ways.

**What happens on each capture**

1. The light face of the card is found and its four corners are built from the dark role bar, so a mild tilt or keystone still lines up. On a light background, where that face blends in, the role bar itself is the landmark.
2. That quad is straightened to the same shape as the template badges.
3. The existing image match runs on the role strip. OCR reads the same strip, limited to Guest, Delegate, Speaker, Crew, and Official.
4. If OCR names one of those words, that word wins, including when the image score is only middling. If OCR gets nothing and the image match still clears its bar, the image match wins. If they name different roles and the image match is only barely ahead, the capture is rejected. A wide gap (0.08 or more) keeps the image match.

OCR starts downloading when the Scan screen opens, then stays in the browser cache. The image match still decides if that download is not finished yet. The engine and English data come from the jsDelivr CDN on the first visit.

**Checked here**

All five roles matched when the card filled the frame, when it sat on black at about 60% of the frame, when it was smaller and off to one side, when it sat on a light background, and when Delegate was rotated or skewed. A blank frame and an orange frame with no badge were rejected. The Scan screen still opens, and its built-in check of the five template badges passes.

I could not point a phone at a physical badge from this browser. A real Capture on the floor is the remaining check, especially a card with background visible around it, like your first photo.
